selected_news.title: Güney Kore, Antalya AI Pledge ile Merkezlere Yeşil Söz
selected_news.summary: "Clean Energy Must Be Supplied to AI and Data Center Infrastructure"... South Korea Joins Antalya AI Pledge 아시아경제

selected_news.source_headline: "Clean Energy Must Be Supplied to AI and Data Center Infrastructure"... South Korea Joins Antalya AI Pledge
selected_news.article_text: On the 16th local time, Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment Kim Seonghwan attends a high-level meeting of the Carbon Market Coalition at the Antalya Expo Center in Antalya, Türkiye, where the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) is being held. Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment South Korea has signed on to the "Antalya AI Pledge," which calls for reducing the environmental burden of the energy and water used by data centers and harnessing AI to combat climate change. The pledge is expected to serve as a tool for climate and environmental groups to pressure the government to strengthen regulations on the electricity and water consumed by data centers According to climate and environmental groups, the South Korean government decided to join the Antalya AI Pledge at the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31), currently taking place in Antalya, Türkiye Türkiye, the COP31 host country, launched the Antalya AI Pledge on November 16 local time in partnership with the International Telecommunication Union (ITU). The Turkish government said that, as of that day, it had secured 80 endorsements and 271 commitments to take action However, only about 10 countries have joined the pledge so far. In addition to South Korea, signatories include Andorra, Brazil, Colombia, Sierra Leone, Somalia, Uganda and Luxembourg The United States, China and the European Union (EU), which account for most investment in AI and data centers, have not signed the pledge. Companies leading the global AI industry, including NVIDIA, OpenAI and Anthropic, have also yet to join, according to reports The Antalya AI Pledge has, however, secured the support of the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD). Amazon, Google and Meta are among its members, but it is unclear whether any of these companies have individually endorsed the pledge The Antalya AI Pledge calls on governments, businesses and organizations to harness AI to address climate change while managing the environmental impact of the energy, water and raw materials consumed by AI. It is nonbinding, and countries may implement it voluntarily The pledge focuses on four main areas: ▲ supplying clean energy to AI and data center infrastructure; ▲ ensuring responsible management throughout the entire AI life cycle, including electronic waste; ▲ measuring and reporting AI's environmental impact; and ▲ expanding developing countries' access to financial and technical capacity and computing resources In particular, the pledge's first provision calls for increasing the share of carbon-free and low-power energy in the electricity used by AI and data center infrastructure; effectively integrating this infrastructure into power grids to help meet growing electricity demand sustainably; and appropriately allocating infrastructure costs associated with data center development, including the expansion of transmission networks The pledge proposes reviewing progress annually at the UN climate change conference through 2030. The first review is expected to begin at COP32. It contains no provisions for penalties to enforce implementation Climate and environmental groups welcomed South Korea's participation and have already begun pressuring the government Lee Seonmi, planning team leader at the People's Solidarity for Participatory Democracy, said, "The South Korean government should use its commitment to the international community as an opportunity to move away from unlimited deregulation and a race to build data centers, and take action toward sustainable and green AI. Specifically, joining the Antalya AI Pledge must lead to amendments to relevant domestic laws and improvements to the regulatory framework." Hwang Sukyoung, secretary-general of Environmental Justice, said, "We welcome the South Korean government's participation in the Antalya AI Pledge and urge it to lead to a fundamental shift in the country's AI data center policy." © The Asia Business Daily.
